name: Disable a machine
summary: An electric or electromagnetic effect stops a machine for a short time without destroying it. Versions differ in what they stop: a pin keeps a vehicle from moving, deploying or transforming while its guns still work; a weapons lock leaves it driving but unable to fire or use abilities; a full shutdown stops both and may also knock out shields, sensors or the crew's display. It comes as a held beam, a fired or thrown pulse, a hack, or a burst around the user. Only machines are affected (vehicles, walkers, drones, turrets, robots); soldiers are immune or only dazzled. It deals little or no damage, so its worth is what the team does in the window: catch, surround or kill the stalled machine. Many area versions stop friendly machines too.
counterplay: Kill or drive off the disabler: most are light support units that must stay close or keep line of sight, with little to fight soldiers with.
Break the link: a beam or hack ends the moment it loses its target, and the machine starts up again.
Spread out, so one pulse stops only one machine.
Fight on with what still works: a pinned vehicle can still turn its gun on the disabler, and soldiers riding in a stalled transport can keep shooting or jump out.
Bring soldiers or aircraft against ground-only disablers: infantry are immune, and most pins and pulses can't reach fliers.
Restore the machine: some versions wear off quickly or can be cured by a medic-style restore, so keep a support player close.

other_examples.note: A quick, thinly armoured vehicle that needs time to charge, then releases a short-range pulse around itself that stops every vehicle, structure and cyborg nearby, its own side's included, for several seconds. Infantry are immune, and firing again doesn't lengthen the effect, so the advice is to pulse once and pull back.

A base building that sends a pulse to a far-off spot of the player's choosing and briefly disables vehicles, structures and cyborgs there. Tunnelling vehicles are forced to the surface, a hover vehicle caught over water sinks, and aircraft in flight are not affected.

Has to stand still and keep a jamming beam on one ground vehicle to paralyse it; the target starts again as soon as the beam is lost, the biggest tanks need several jammers at once, and soldiers riding in a paralysed transport can still shoot. While it jams a vehicle it can't deflect incoming missiles, its other job.
A hack that shuts down one enemy ground vehicle from a short distance; using it gives away the stealthed hacker, so it works best on isolated vehicles.

A defensive missile battery whose missiles also release a pulse that leaves vehicles immobile for a while; aircraft that are hit drop out of the sky, and the pulse catches friendly vehicles in its area as well.

A long-range missile that can't be dodged once fired; it stops one mechanical or psionic unit from attacking or using abilities for several seconds, but the target can still move, and a struck transport can't load or unload. Players aim it at the enemy's most valuable machines.

sources.title: Raven (Legacy of the Void), Liquipedia StarCraft II Wiki

other_examples.note: Shorts out one mechanical unit for a long time: it can't move, fire or take orders, though it can still be attacked or repaired, and a medic's restoration ability cures it. Biological units are immune, so it does nothing against an all-organic army.

sources.title: Lockdown, Liquipedia StarCraft Brood War Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: An overcharged plasma pistol shot briefly disables a vehicle and strips energy shields; some disabled vehicles keep a working turret. Halo Infinite moved the vehicle effect to shock weapons that need sustained fire, and a later remake brought the pistol's version back.

A thrown grenade that does almost no damage but shuts down or slows vehicles and electronic devices nearby for a few seconds; in 2142 a player with a supply of grenades could keep one vehicle down for a long time. In 2042 affected vehicles can't fire or use equipment, players' HUDs fizzle, and repeated pulses can destroy placed gadgets.

sources.title: EMP Grenade, Battlefield Wiki
sources.note: Quotes the Battlefield 2042 in-game description and the Battlefield 2142 Prima guide.

shooter_analogues.note: An electric grenade that scrambles the vision displays of Titans and pilots and drains a Titan's shield while doing little hull damage; robot soldiers short-circuit and drop for a moment. It sets Titans up for anti-Titan weapons and gives pilots time to get away.
In the co-op mode the Spy's sapper stuns robots for a few seconds (giant robots are only slowed) and then needs to recharge before its next use.

player_translation.summary: A support or skirmisher tool that stops one enemy machine, or a small group, for a short and clearly shown window so teammates can kill or slip past it. The disabler gives up damage for control, and the machine's driver always keeps something to do.
as_user: Hold the beam on an enemy vehicle in range to pin it, or fire or throw a pulse that stops the machines in a small circle.
Your effect does little or no damage: ping the stalled target and let your team finish it.
A beam needs line of sight and stays within a capped range, so you are exposed while you hold it.
Pulses also stop your own team's machines in the area, so place them with care.
Soldiers are immune, so you pick your targets: tanks, walkers, drones, turrets.
as_target: An 'EMP' or 'pinned' banner with a timer ring and a marker pointing at the source; the vehicle visibly sparks.

Pinned, you can't move but can still aim and fire, so shoot the disabler. Weapons-locked, you can drive to cover. A full shutdown comes only from T2 and is short, and you can bail out (hold X) and fight on foot.
A beam is a tether: hold F to shake it off after a moment, or break line of sight.
When the effect ends you get a few seconds of immunity, so nobody can chain-lock you.
teammates: Setup and finish: the disabler pins, anti-armour teammates kill; it also sets up infesters and boarders.
Passengers matter: soldiers riding a stalled transport can still shoot from it or jump out and fight.
Repair and support classes shorten a disable on a friendly machine.
Defenders screen their vehicles with anti-infantry escorts and spotters that catch disablers early.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse is the main weapon.
Beam variant: hold right mouse on the machine under the cursor (the secondary weapon slot); the range cap is drawn as a ring around you, and releasing ends it.
Pulse variant: Q fires or throws the pulse at the cursor (or around yourself for the burst variant), on a cooldown.
Victim, with the universal keys: hold F to shake off a beam or hack, even while pinned; hold X to bail out of a shut-down vehicle.
The pattern uses one counted key (right mouse or Q), within any tier's budget.
feedback: A crackling blue beam, or a visible expanding ring for pulses, and sparks and a stalled-engine sound on the affected machine.
A countdown ring over the disabled machine that both teams see from above, followed by a short immunity shimmer.
The victim's HUD says what is off (movement, weapons or both), not just 'disabled'.
Pulse areas are drawn on the ground before they land, in the thrower's team colour, so friendly drivers can get out of the way.
Units that can be affected carry a small machine icon, so players know who counts as a machine.
changes_from_rts: RTS disables can last a long time (StarCraft's Lockdown holds for most of a minute); a player locked that long just waits, so here they last a few seconds and are followed by immunity.
A full shutdown is a stun for vehicles, so under decision 5B it comes only from T2, stays short and sits on a medium or longer cooldown, and the victim can bail out.
In the RTS the ray holds its target for as long as the drone keeps it on; here the beam is a tether the victim can shake off, so it is a window, not a lock.
RTS pulses that also stop your own units are fine for strategy; in a team shooter the area is shown before it lands so teammates can avoid it.
Players can't check unit stats, so which units count as machines must be shown with an icon.
Aircraft that crash when hit (Zero Hour's EMP Patriot) would be an instant kill; here fliers are forced to settle onto the ground, or are not affected.

team_play.notes: A pure setup tool: the disabler creates the window and anti-armour teammates convert it. Vehicle-heavy teams have to escort their machines and pick soldiers or aircraft that are immune or out of reach.

notes: Status effects with timers (no moving, no firing, or both) plus an immunity window, applied only to units tagged as machines.
A beam needs range and line-of-sight checks and breaks on shake-off; a pulse needs an area preview and friendly-fire rules.
Interactions to handle: passengers who keep firing, deploy and transform locks, shields switched off, fliers forced down.
UI on both sides: the victim's banner and countdown, the disabler's beam range ring, and area previews.
Several disablers taking turns can lock a vehicle for good (a Battlefield 2142 player with resupply could keep one down indefinitely); immunity after each disable and shorter repeats prevent it.
Cheap T1 disablers can make expensive T3 vehicles useless; shorten the effect on bigger targets, as Zero Hour needed several jammers for its heaviest tanks.
An area pulse on an objective can stop a whole push; the friendly-fire rule and a visible warning keep it fair.
Against a team of soldiers the pattern does nothing, so a card with it needs another use.
Players must see what is disabled: movement, weapons or both.
A pinned vehicle that still fires looks healthy from above; sparks and a ring must make the state obvious.
A friendly pulse that stops your own vehicles must be readable before it lands.

variants.name: Pinning beam
variants.summary: A held beam keeps one ground machine from moving, deploying or transforming while its guns still work; it ends when the beam breaks or the victim shakes it off.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 3 terror drone stasis ray

variants.name: Weapons lock
variants.summary: A missile or hack stops one machine from firing and using abilities for a few seconds; it can still drive away.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Raven interference matrix, Battlefield 2042 EMP grenade

variants.name: Shutdown pulse
variants.summary: A fired or thrown pulse stops every machine in a small area, friend or foe, from moving and firing for a short time.
variants.seen_in: Tiberian Sun EMP cannon, Battlefield 2142 EMP grenade, Zero Hour EMP Patriot

variants.name: Charged burst
variants.summary: After a visible charge-up you release a pulse around yourself; you can carry the charge while you close in, and you are not affected by your own burst.

variants.name: Scramble systems
variants.summary: Little stopping power: it blinds the machine's display and minimap for a moment and drains its shield, opening it up to anti-armour fire.
variants.seen_in: Titanfall arc grenade, Halo plasma pistol overcharge (shields)

variants.name: Clamp-on stunner
variants.summary: A device stuck onto a machine stops it until a short timer ends or the device is knocked off, then must recharge.
variants.seen_in: Team Fortress 2 Mann vs. Machine sapper

variants.name: Forced landing
variants.summary: A low flier that is hit loses lift and settles to the ground for a few seconds, where ground weapons can reach it, instead of crashing.
variants.seen_in: Zero Hour EMP Patriot (aircraft crash outright there)

adds_strengths.why: Stops an enemy machine from moving or firing for a few seconds, so the team can catch it or kill it.

adds_weaknesses.why: Does nothing to soldiers and little damage to anything, so it needs teammates to turn the window into a kill.

counters.why: Tanks, walkers and other crewed machines stall in place or go quiet while the effect lasts.
Drones, robots and turrets are machines through and through and stop just the same.
A pinned machine can't transform or deploy, so it is stuck in its current form.

countered_by.why: Soldiers are immune, and the disabler usually has little to hurt them with.
Most pins and pulses only reach ground machines, so fliers can attack the disabler freely.

open_questions: How long may a full shutdown last at T2 and T3 under decision 5B, and does an immunity window after each disable stop chain-locks well enough?
Should pulses also stop friendly machines, as in Tiberian Sun and Zero Hour?
What happens to an aircraft that is hit: a forced landing, a slow drift, or no effect at all?
Should soldiers be dazzled (a scrambled HUD, as with Titanfall's arc grenade) or fully immune?

shooter_fit.reason: Battlefield and Halo already use EMP grenades and overcharged shots against vehicles, and a short, readable window that teammates turn into a kill is good team play. Long or chained lockdowns frustrate, so they must stay short.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. The wrong paths were fixed as the skeptic confirmed (cbe6de8).
